paper_title: Direct Detection of Dark Photon Dark Matter with the James Webb Space Telescope
notes: This paper is a PROJECTED sensitivity, not a measured limit: the authors show that the current in-space JWST configuration cannot detect DPDM-induced photons, and propose a modified mirror configuration usable during ground testing of future space telescopes (LUVOIR, HabEx, Origins, Roman). Using JWST NIRSpec/MIRI parameters and real noise data from 972 observation projects, they project 95% C.L. upper limits of epsilon ~ 1e-12 to 1e-14 over 10-500 THz (mass 4.14e-2 to 2.07 eV, converted via m[eV]=4.136e-15*f[Hz]). No detailed numerical table is provided; the two data points are a rough bracket of the stated range from the abstract/text (the actual Fig. 4 dashed curve is not machine-readable here, and the assignment of which coupling value corresponds to which mass endpoint is uncertain). Local DM density assumed via rho_DM in Eq. (2.4) but numerical value not stated in the provided text, so dm_density_assumed left null (standard halo model with v0=235 km/s, vesc~500 km/s is used). | [VISION GATE A] is_projection=true but the vision notes say the traced curve is existing experiment 'jwst' — not the paper's own projected curve | selector: text (sole candidate)
